record.field: Discover what you can do, inspect model schemas, and read the business context that explains what the data means.
Search, count, resolve names and aggregate any model the connection is scoped to — the foundation for questions, reports and dashboards.
Create, update and delete records. Hidden entirely from read-only scopes and optionally routed through human approval.
List the capabilities and tools available to this connection, and whether it is read-only. Call this first to learn what you can do.
List the Odoo models this connection may access and which operations (read, create, write, delete) are permitted on each.
Return the fields of a model (label, type, help, relation) so you can build correct domains and value dictionaries. Blacklisted fields are omitted.
Return admin-authored, plain-language context that explains what a model or the company means in business terms. Use it to reason correctly about workflows.

Search a model with an Odoo domain and read fields back. The domain is a list-of-tuples given as a string. Results respect the user permissions and the scope row cap.

Count records matching an Odoo domain, without reading them. Cheap and safe for large models.
Resolve a text query to record ids and display names — the reliable way to turn a customer or product name into an id before searching or writing.

Aggregate a model by one or more fields and compute measures (sum, avg, count). This powers reports and dashboards, e.g. revenue by month or open leads by salesperson. Date fields accept a granularity suffix like create_date:month.

Create a record from a values object. Subject to the scope: may be blocked, may strip blacklisted fields, and may be routed to human approval instead of executing.
Update one record by id with a values object. The target must satisfy the scope record domain. May be routed to human approval.
Delete one record by id. The target must satisfy the scope record domain. May be routed to human approval.

Run a business action on existing records, such as confirming a quotation or posting an invoice. Only methods an administrator has explicitly allow-listed for that model can be called; everything else is refused. Call get_schema or ask the user if you are unsure which action applies. These actions change business state and are frequently irreversible, so prefer describing what you are about to do and why before calling.
